title: DHCP: Automatic IP Assignment

steps.objective: Enter privileged mode to explore DHCP
steps.teachingPoint: DHCP stands for Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol - it's like a receptionist that hands out addresses to visitors!
Without DHCP, you'd have to manually type an IP address on every single computer, phone, and tablet. Imagine doing that for 500 devices!
Think of DHCP like a school giving out locker numbers - students don't pick their own lockers, they get assigned one automatically!

steps.objective: View the LAN interface (where devices connect)
steps.teachingPoint: The LAN interface connects to devices that need IP addresses - computers, phones, printers, and more.

steps.objective: Give this interface an IP address (this will be the gateway)
steps.teachingPoint: This IP (192.168.100.1) becomes the 'default gateway' - the exit door for all traffic leaving your network.
Just like a light switch - you need to turn it ON for it to work!
Now our router's LAN port has an address. Next, we'd set up DHCP to give out addresses to other devices.
A DHCP 'pool' is like a bucket of addresses the router can hand out. Each pool has a name and a range of addresses.
A DHCP pool configuration would include: 1) The network range (which addresses to give out), 2) The gateway (where to send traffic), 3) DNS servers (for looking up websites).

steps.objective: Enter configuration mode to discuss exclusions
steps.teachingPoint: Some IP addresses should NEVER be given out by DHCP - like the router itself! These are called 'excluded addresses'.
You typically exclude: The router's IP, server IPs, printer IPs - anything that needs a permanent, unchanging address.
DORA = Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge. When your laptop connects to WiFi, it goes through these 4 steps to get an IP!
DISCOVER: Device shouts 'I need an IP!' - OFFER: Router says 'How about 192.168.100.50?' - REQUEST: Device says 'Yes, I'll take it!' - ACKNOWLEDGE: Router confirms 'It's yours!'

assertions.description: Configuration must be saved with 'write memory'
G0/1 should have IP 192.168.100.1 (the gateway address for DHCP clients)

legacyCommands: ! DHCP CONFIGURATION REFERENCE
! When this feature is implemented, you'll use these commands:
! STEP 1: Exclude addresses that should NOT be given out
! ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.100.1 192.168.100.10
! ^ This reserves .1 through .10 for routers/servers
! STEP 2: Create a DHCP pool
! ip dhcp pool SCHOOL_NETWORK
!   default-router 192.168.100.1
!   dns-server 8.8.8.8
! WHAT EACH LINE MEANS:
! - pool name: Any name you want (SCHOOL_NETWORK, LAN_POOL, etc.)
! - network: The subnet to assign addresses FROM
! - default-router: The gateway IP (usually the router's LAN IP)
! - dns-server: Where to look up website names (8.8.8.8 is Google's)
! RESULT: Devices get IPs from 192.168.100.11 to 192.168.100.254
! KEY CONCEPTS FOR MIDDLE SCHOOLERS
! Q: Why do we EXCLUDE addresses?
! A: So the router doesn't accidentally give away the router's
!    own IP address, or addresses we want for servers/printers!
! Q: What is a 'lease'?
! A: DHCP addresses are temporary - like checking out a library
!    book. After the lease expires, the device asks for renewal.
! Q: What's the difference between STATIC and DHCP?
! A: Static = you type the IP yourself (permanent)
!    DHCP = the router gives you an IP automatically (temporary)
! DORA - The Four Steps:
! D = Discover (device: 'Anyone have an IP for me?')
! O = Offer (server: 'Here's 192.168.100.50!')
! R = Request (device: 'I'll take that one!')
! A = Acknowledge (server: 'Done! It's yours for 24 hours.')
